newsitem.title: FRANCE: Judge questions Paris mayor over payment to wife.
newsitem.headline: Judge questions Paris mayor over payment to wife.

text.p: An investigating magistrate questioned Paris Gaullist mayor Jean Tiberi on Friday over alleged misuse of public funds.

Tiberi emerged from the lawcourts in the Paris suburb of Evry after nearly two and a half hours of questioning about an alleged payment made to his wife and deposited in their joint bank account, but made no comment to waiting reporters.

He was placed under investigation earlier this month over the suspected payment of 200,000 francs ($35,000) to his wife by the elected council of Essonne near Paris in exchange for a 36-page report largely copied out of a book.
Xaviere Tiberi is also under investigation concerning the payment for the report, which is on prospects for economic links to French-speaking nations. She was questioned in Evry on Thursday.

Jean Tiberi is also under fire in a probe into suspected illicit funding of his RPR party by Paris municipal housing authority and a scandal over the letting of city-owned flats to political cronies and family members at lower than market rents.
Tiberi, who succeeded President Jacques Chirac as the capital's mayor when his mentor was elected in 1995, has denied any wrongdoing and has vowed to stay in office.
